item.title: AI robot may stop your dog from barking while you're gone
item.description: WIM-Z's AI dog training robot uses on-device processing to detect barking and dispense treats autonomously, with field trials showing up to 83% reduction.
item.content:encoded:
If your dog starts barking the second you walk out the door, leaving home can come with a little extra guilt. That can happen whether you live in an apartment or a house. A pet camera can show you what is happening, but watching from your phone does little when your dog reacts to every sound outside or gets anxious when you are gone.

WIM-Z wants to take a more active role. The small tracked robot uses on-device artificial intelligence to watch your dog and respond to certain behaviors. Once the robot is in position, it can identify your dog, detect barking and decide when to reward calmer behavior with a treat. You can also speak through the robot and drive it around your home from your phone.

AI ROBOT FOR SENIORS CAN ALERT FAMILY AFTER A CALL FOR HELP

Now WIM-Z has shared early field results, and its first customer units will make behavior and training decisions on their own while owners control where the robot moves.

NEW! 🩺 Free CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI Saturday, September 26 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com

WIM-Z stands for Watchful Intelligent Mobile Zen. The robot measures about 11 inches tall and rides on rubber tank-style treads. Its camera turret can pan 270 degrees and tilt more than 120 degrees. A side cartridge holds up to 44 treats.

Inside, WIM-Z uses a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-8 AI accelerator. The company says its onboard AI can identify individual dogs, classify barking and track a dog with its pan-and-tilt camera.

Once WIM-Z detects barking, its behavior system can decide whether to intervene without waiting for you. The robot can then use a calming cue and dispense a treat when appropriate.

However, there is an important limit. WIM-Z does not currently drive itself around your home looking for your dog. You control that movement through the app, or you can leave the robot in one location.

WIM-Z also includes two-way audio. Its app can show behavior activity and optional highlight clips, giving you another way to see what happened while you were away.

WIM-Z recently released results from seven field trials conducted between May and September 2026. Six took place in homes around the New York metro area. One took place at a kennel in Jersey City. Across the trials, four hand-built robots logged 50 sessions and about 60 hours of use. WIM-Z says the system detected more than 2,100 barks. It also made 107 autonomous interventions and dispensed about 500 rewards.

The biggest numbers came from two homes that ran repeat autonomous sessions over two to three weeks. In one home, barking fell from 161 barks per hour to 40, a 75% reduction. In the other, barking fell from 317 barks per hour to 53, an 83% reduction. WIM-Z also reported that more interventions ended with the dogs going quiet as the trials progressed.

ROBOT DOG COULD DELIVER YOUR NEXT PACKAGE AND AN AD

WIM-Z takes a gentler approach. Instead of using shocks, sprays or scolding, it relies on treats and calm cues to reinforce better behavior. That lines up with guidance from the American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior, which recommends reward-based training and warns against aversive methods.

The bigger question is whether the AI can read the situation well enough to respond appropriately. A dog barking at a delivery person is very different from one that is distressed because you left. WIM-Z has to recognize that difference and react at the right moment for the approach to work well.

WIM-Z can handle the behavior side on its own. Its onboard AI can identify a dog, track it with the pan-and-tilt camera, detect barking, decide when to intervene and dispense a reward without you making each decision. What it cannot do yet is navigate your home on its own. You drive WIM-Z from room to room through the app, or you can leave it in one spot where your dog spends time.

The first customer units will work this way, combining autonomous behavior and training features with owner-controlled movement. Full self-navigation, where the robot maps your home and goes looking for your dog by itself, remains on the company's roadmap and will not be included in the first units. So, WIM-Z can decide how to respond to your dog, but you still decide where the robot goes.

Any mobile robot with a camera and microphone deserves a privacy check before you let it roam around your living room. We asked WIM-Z exactly what happens to the information it collects. The company says all AI processing happens on the robot itself. That includes behavior detection, bark classification and decisions about when to intervene. No video is sent to the cloud for AI analysis.

Some information can still leave the robot. Event data such as bark activity, behavior interventions, treat dispensing and battery status are stored on an Amazon Web Services relay server so it can appear in the app's activity history. If you connect remotely, live video and two-way audio stream through WIM-Z's relay using encrypted WebRTC technology. The company says these are live streams to your phone, not recordings, and they are not stored on its servers.

Optional highlight clips work differently. Short selected clips can be uploaded for assembly and playback in the app, but WIM-Z says continuous footage is never uploaded. Owners can delete clips at any time or turn the feature off completely. The company says those clips are deleted within 90 days after an account is deleted.

WIM-Z also told CyberGuy that it does not sell customer data. Customer footage is not used to train its AI models unless the owner explicitly opts in. When the robot is used only on local Wi-Fi without remote access, the company says nothing leaves the home.

We have raised similar questions with other connected home robots because a camera that can move around your house gets access to very private spaces. Those answers give us a much clearer idea of how WIM-Z handles your information. Still, I would review the privacy controls before bringing any connected camera into my home.

ONE-WHEELED AI SECURITY ROBOT COULD PATROL YOUR PROPERTY

WIM-Z will cost $799 for the first production units. Right now, the company is taking a fully refundable $99 deposit to hold a spot. WIM-Z told CyberGuy it expects the first batch to ship from late Q4 2026 through Q1 2027. That means the first units could arrive between the end of 2026 and early 2027.

The company also acknowledges that hardware schedules can slip. If WIM-Z has not shipped your unit by Q2 2027, it says your deposit will be refunded automatically. WIM-Z says the deposits are held through Stripe and are not placed in the company's operating account.

The company says it has built five robots so far. Four are still being used in the field, while another is in Shenzhen, China, for production evaluation with a manufacturer. That gives you a pretty good sense of where things stand. WIM-Z is still in the early stages, so reserving one now means you are getting in before the product has been widely released and used in homes.

If your dog tends to bark or get restless when you leave, WIM-Z shows where pet tech may be headed next. Instead of simply alerting you that something is happening, the robot can respond while you are away by using a calming cue and rewarding your dog when it settles down.

There is one thing to remember with the first version. WIM-Z will not roam around your house looking for your dog by itself. You will need to position it where your dog spends time or drive it remotely through the app.

Still, I would not count on a robot to solve serious separation anxiety. The ASPCA says dogs with moderate or severe separation anxiety may need gradual behavior work with an experienced professional. For barking or mild restlessness, though, a robot that recognizes what your dog is doing and responds at the right time could be a useful extra set of eyes at home.

The early results are interesting, but I want to see what happens when WIM-Z is tested with many more dogs in different homes. I also want to see how well the first production units perform once customers start using them. For now, WIM-Z has an interesting idea, some encouraging early numbers and a much clearer picture of what buyers will actually get.

WIM-Z caught my attention because it tackles a problem pet cameras mostly leave in your hands. Seeing your dog bark from miles away can make you feel helpless. WIM-Z's onboard AI can make a training decision and reward calm behavior without waiting for you to step in. I also like that the first version keeps movement in your hands. You control where the robot goes, while the behavior and training system can operate on its own. Full self-navigation may come later. Keeping the AI processing on the robot means your video does not need to go to the cloud for behavior analysis. Remote features and optional highlight clips can still send some information outside your home, so you will want to understand those settings. At $799, I would still want to see more testing and hear from real customers once the first production units start shipping. But if WIM-Z can build on these early results, it could become a useful tool for dog owners who worry about what happens after they walk out the door.

Would you trust an AI robot to decide when your dog needs a calming cue or treat while you are away? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Granddaughter says grandma rejected MAID before lethal procedure, ‘I don’t want the death shot’
item.description: Brigitte Stegemann's granddaughter alleges the 83-year-old had no idea she was about to die until she was told a lethal MAID injection was scheduled.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 800-273-TALK (8255).

The granddaughter of an 83-year-old Canadian woman who died through the country’s assisted-death program in July says her grandmother had no idea she was about to die until she was told she would be given a lethal injection just days prior.

Brigitte Kranendonk, who cared for her grandmother Brigitte Stegemann, says the family cut short a vacation after learning that the long-term care home had scheduled a second MAiD assessment, despite Stegemann previously declining the procedure.

"Just before we had come back from our vacation, I received a phone call from the home stating that they had booked a second assessment for MAiD to happen with my grandmother, and at this point my Oma had already denied MAiD," Kranendonk told Fox News Digital in an interview Tuesday. "When we went to the home after our vacation – we did cut it short, we came home, we saw her. She had no idea what was happening."

DEMENTIA STOLE MY GRANDMOTHER FROM US. I AM FIGHTING TO GIVE FAMILIES MORE TIME

Kranendonk said that she was her grandmother’s primary caregiver and that her family had decided to place Stegemann at The Pearl care home in Cannifton due to physical and mental decline.

Her grandmother, however, still had a good appetite and was in good spirits even following a stomach cancer diagnosis, and rejected the idea of using MAiD when it was presented as an option.

"She had an opportunity to get an IV port, meaning for injectable medicine. They didn't have to re-poke her every time," Kranendonk said. "It was kind of a one-and-done deal. She had ripped it out several times because she kept saying, ‘I don't want the death shot.’"

"And it wasn't until I, face to face, explained it to her that this is not what it is, this is just pain management," Kranendonk added. "That was the scary part is that it felt like she went from screaming, 'I don't want the death shot,' to then accepting MAiD. But only while I was on vacation."

EXCLUSIVE: ‘BROKEN COUNTRY’ FILMMAKER WARNS CANADA’S SLOW DECLINE OFFERS CAUTIONARY TALE FOR AMERICANS

Stegemann was killed under Canada’s physician-assisted suicide program, called Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD), on July 10.

Kranendonk says her grandmother’s first language was not English and that she was severely hearing impaired.

"My grandmother's first language is not English," Kranendonk said. "She is severely hearing impaired. And she, her whole life, was terrified of feeling dumb. She never wanted to look as if she didn't understand what was going on. And so when the doctor came in and was explaining MAiD and using very loose terms, like, ‘We're just going to give you medicine, you're not going to feel pain. And don't worry, you won't have a bowel movement,’ my grandma's just sitting there nodding. And I stopped, and I said to her, ‘She doesn't understand what you're saying.’"

When Kranendonk directly asked Stegemann whether she knew she would die that Friday, she said her grandmother was visibly shocked and cried for roughly 45 minutes, repeatedly saying, "I made a mistake."

NEW YORK NUNS WILL NOT BE FORCED TO COMPLY WITH ASSISTED-SUICIDE LAW WHILE CASE PROGRESSES

The doctor had allegedly said Stegemann could "deny" MAiD on the day of the procedure, but Stegemann was already unsure if her grandmother had actually consented to it in the first place.

The day the procedure occurred, Kranendonk said the nurse who was administering the IV was not wearing gloves and had a hard time putting it into her right arm, piercing her grandmother many times.

"I'm not a nurse," Kranendonk said. "I've never done an IV. I've seen them done before. There was so much blood with this IV. It was all over her arm, it was soaking through her nighty, it was all over the pillow. And it was all over the nurse's hands. And at that moment when I saw all the blood all over the nurse's hands, I realized the nurse was not even wearing gloves."

Kranendonk also alleges that Stegemann did not verbally acknowledge the doctor’s final question before the procedure was started.

NEW YORK NUNS' CHALLENGE TO ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW IS ABOUT PROTECTING FREEDOM, LAWYER SAYS

"And the doctor comes in and says, I can't remember exactly how she worded it, but it was something like, ‘Good morning, Brigitte, are you OK if we proceed with MAiD,’ or, ‘Are you OK if we proceed?’ I can't remember what she asked my Oma. My Oma doesn't say anything. No acknowledgment, no head nod, nothing. Just lying there with her eyes closed. And the doctor says, ‘OK, we're going to proceed.’"

Kranendonk said the family is seeking investigations by the coroner’s office, an ombudsman and the long-term care action line.

ASSISTED LIVING CENTER SENT RESIDENT TO DOCTOR'S APPOINTMENT AFTER GIVING HIM 18 SHOTS, 5 AM BEER: OFFICIALS

"With the investigation with the coroner's office, the ombudsman, the long-term care action line, there's essentially two streams here that we're asking to be investigated under," Kranendonk said. "One is the part of the home, and the part that the home had played in this, and then also the MAiD process. The home had taken it upon themselves to fill out the paperwork, witness and get my Oma to sign off. I don't know what the conversation was that they had with her while she was signing the paperwork, I don't know if she even knew that it was the MAiD paperwork for it."

On its website, The Pearl care home in Cannifton, where Stegemann lived, says that it currently has 57 licensed beds with 86 people on the waiting list.

Fox News Digital reached out to The Pearl and Belleville Police for comment but did not immediately hear back.

item.title: Yankees' World Series hopes take major hit as Aaron Judge may not be on postseason roster with calf injury
item.description: New York Yankees star Aaron Judge received a platelet-poor plasma injection in his right calf, and Aaron Boone said he's not expected for the postseason.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees may have a Judge-sized hole in their lineup for the postseason.

Aaron Judge had a platelet-poor plasma injection into his right calf during the team’s off day on Monday following its return from Arizona, manager Aaron Boone said. The injection puts his status for the postseason in doubt.

"We’re planning on him not being a part of that, but we’re also at [that] time of the year, you hear all the time with injuries, you give ranges two to four weeks, four to six weeks," Boone said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"The range is for a reason, and we’re at a point of the year where obviously we push it a little bit if that was in play, but that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out either."

After just seven games following his return from a rib injury that kept him out of the lineup for three months, Judge was placed back on the injured list with a calf strain last week. He is eligible to be activated on the final day of the regular season in the Yankees’ series against the Baltimore Orioles, but an activation appears unlikely.

Judge injured his calf in the Yankees’ final game of their series against the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday. He was pinch-hit for in the sixth inning and said after the game that the move was precautionary.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Boone said symptoms persisted, and an MRI revealed the strain.

While Judge might not have been hitting like himself in his seven games back, going 4 for 23 with one home run and 13 strikeouts, his presence in the lineup was a boost. Even when the three-time AL MVP isn’t hitting, Judge’s presence in the lineup takes pressure off other hitters.

With Judge in the lineup, the Yankees are 41-25, while they are 48-41 without him. While the Yankees managed to remain above .500 without Judge in the lineup, their offense cratered in his absence. The team’s pitching staff, and their MLB-leading 3.22 ERA have carried the load without the eight-time All-Star.

In 66 games this season, Judge is hitting .241 with 18 home runs and 41 RBI.

The Yankees are likely to play the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card series for the second straight season at home in the Bronx. While the Yankees would love to have Judge in the lineup, Boone said the expectation doesn’t change.

"We’ve played much of the year without him and, for the most part, we’ve done a pretty good job," Boone said. "So guys are used to it. Obviously, you always want your best player in the mix, but we understand we’ve got a job to do and an expectation to win. I think that expectation doesn’t change with or without him. We’re expecting to go into the series and know we can beat anyone when we play our game."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump ally skips UNGA for first time — months after face-to-face with president gave way to bitter clash
item.description: Giorgia Meloni's decision to skip the United Nations General Assembly follows an escalating public feud with Trump over G7 and NATO encounters.
item.content:encoded:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is not attending the United Nations General Assembly this week, an official confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Meloni’s decision not to attend breaks with a roughly 15-year stretch in which an Italian prime minister took part in the U.N. General Assembly’s annual high-level debate, according to Associated Medias, although the 2020 gathering was held largely virtually because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Meloni said she will not attend the UNGA, citing a packed schedule after attending six summits in three and a half weeks and saying she had "several dossiers" to handle at home.

Meloni’s absence also means the two leaders will avoid another face-to-face encounter after recent international summits put their growing tensions on public display, despite a previously warm relationship.

WORLD LEADERS DESCEND ON NEW YORK FOR UNGA — BUT WHO REALLY HAS AMERICA’S EAR?

"We believe the United Nations the basic instrument for achieving peace everywhere. Indeed we want a stronger role United Nations, we are present at many initiatives and we have an Italian candidate at the helm of the FAO", Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said ahead of the summit, according to Italian outlet ANSA. "There is great attention from the Italian side."

Their spat escalated in June after Trump said Meloni had "begged" him to take a photo at the G7, months after tensions first surfaced publicly when Meloni opposed U.S. military action against Iran and called Trump’s criticism of Pope Leo XIV "unacceptable."

The two leaders have long had a warmer relationship than Trump has shared with many other U.S. allies, with Meloni notably the only European leader to attend his 2025 presidential inauguration.

In July, Meloni and Trump feuded in the lead up to the NATO summit in Turkey after Trump posted "RESTRAINING ORDER NEEDED," on Truth, alongside a photo of Meloni looking at him.

TRUMP-MELONI SPAT GROWS OVER CLAIM ITALIAN PM 'BEGGED' FOR PHOTO: 'ASTONISHED'

"Trump's statements against Meloni speak for themselves," Tajani said in July while at a Sky TG24 event. "We are convinced that transatlantic relations go far beyond individual statements."

The exchange followed a June interview with Italy’s La7 after the G7, when Trump mocked Meloni over what he claimed was her eagerness to take a photo with him.

"She wanted a picture with me so ​badly. I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her," Trump said at the time to La7 TV channel. "She's probably happy I talked to her. I didn't have to talk to her."

Meloni fired back: "I can only say it is disappointing that he does not show the same determination with the enemies of the West and of the United States, whose leaders he instead treats with far greater indulgence."

RUBIO TO VISIT ITALY, VATICAN AMID TROOP DRAWDOWN CALL, TENSION WITH TRUMP, POPE LEO: REPORTS

"There is one thing he should remember: neither I nor Italy ever beg," she added.

There have been looming tensions between the two leaders after Meloni distanced herself from the U.S. amid mounting domestic and political pressure over the widening Middle East conflict.

Trump also criticized Meloni for failing to assist the U.S. without letting U.S. forces use Italy's landing strips and runways, calling it "a great logistical inconvenience."

"She is doing poorly in Italy with her level of popularity, possibly because she turned down the United States of America, a Country that truly loves and protects Italy, when it came to denying Iran from obtaining or developing a Nuclear Weapon (But so did NATO, for that matter!)," he wrote in June.

TRUMP TAUNTS MELONI WITH FRESH PHOTO SALVO AS NATO SUMMIT PUTS ALLIES FACE-TO-FACE

Italy remains a key U.S. security hub in Europe, hosting nearly 13,000 active-duty American service members as of December 2025, according to Defense Manpower Data Center figures, with personnel based in Vicenza, Aviano, Naples and Sicily.

A senior administration official highlighted President Trump’s meetings with other heads of state and engagement with Gulf partners on Iran when asked by Fox News Digital about Meloni’s absence from the conference.

Tajani is expected to speak at the conference on Wednesday.

item.title: Sister of missing DC mom speaks out after ex’s arrest exposes 'horrifying' abusive relationship
item.description: Antoinette Forbes’ former partner was arrested last week, but authorities have not confirmed whether his case is connected to her disappearance.
item.content:encoded:
The sister of missing D.C. mother Antoinette Forbes revealed that she was unaware Antoinette had been in an abusive relationship until details of a 2021 assault surfaced following the arrest of the father of her 10-year-old son.

Russell Ashford, 65, who was detained last week in Pennsylvania, reportedly took unauthorized overnight custody of their son on the night Antoinette was last seen, according to the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office. He also allegedly violated his probation stemming from the 2021 assault case, the office said. Authorities did not name Ashford as a suspect in Antoinette's disappearance.

"Antoinette did not tell us at all about the assault in 2021, so just wrapping our minds around that, it's unfathomable. We can't really conceive it," Antoinette’s sister, Aileen, said in an interview with Fox News Digital.

"I didn't hear about them until I saw some excerpts of the report after my sister went missing."

FAMILY OF CRITICALLY MISSING DC MOTHER SAYS POLICE STILL TREATING HOME AS ACTIVE CRIME SCENE

According to Maryland court filings, Ashford pleaded guilty to first-degree assault in 2021.

During an argument over their child's schooling, Ashford allegedly threw Antoinette against the staircase, repeatedly punched her while she was lying on the kitchen floor and banged her head against the ground at least a dozen times until she lost consciousness, according to court filings. 

The assault continued until a neighbor heard her screaming and entered the home to intervene.

After Antoinette was taken to a hospital, tests showed she suffered multiple facial lacerations, multiple fractured facial bones, eye damage, a concussion, a broken finger and bruising, court documents said. Prosecutors said the assault left Antoinette with permanent eye and hand injuries.

After pleading guilty, Ashford was sentenced to 15 years in prison but served only nine months and five years' probation upon release, authorities said.

Aileen said the reports came as a shock to her and her family, who are still processing the revelation.

"The report is horrifying. And to tell the truth, I haven't had the time to fully process that. Just the thought of my sister enduring such a brutal attack is just deeply hurtful to me and to the rest of my family. We don't want to, we can't even conceive of it," Aileen said.

FEDS PLAN NEW BAHAMAS SEARCH FOR LYNETTE HOOKER AFTER GPS DATA ALLEGEDLY TORPEDOES HUSBAND’S STORY: SOURCE

Aileen noted that Antoinette may have kept the abuse from her family because she was protective of the people she loved.

"Antoinette, she wanted to protect us from it. She did not want us to have any involvement with Russell," Aileen said.

More than two weeks have passed since Antoinette was last seen on Friday, Sept. 4, just one week before she planned to take her son to visit their relatives in California, Aileen said. 

Antoinette was reported missing on Sept. 6 after friends found her dog, car, phone and wallet inside the home, but no sign of her.

Shortly after her disappearance, Ashford was arrested for allegedly violating his probation, which strictly prohibited him from having hostile contact with Antoinette or their child, amid the concerning circumstances surrounding Antoinette's disappearance, court documents said. 

On July 16, 2026, Ashford reportedly arrived unannounced at his son's summer camp, but staff informed him he was not on the approved pickup list and asked for identification. Ashford allegedly became agitated and forceful with a counselor, prompting staff to file a formal written report about the incident.

Pennsylvania State Police told Fox News Digital that Ashford was arrested after a traffic stop revealed he had an active warrant tied to the July incident.

Authorities told Fox News Digital last week that the search for Antoinette is ongoing and that officials do not have any updates to share with the public.

Aileen further urged anyone living in the Nebraska Avenue Northwest neighborhood where Antoinette lived to check their security cameras and think back to anything that may have seemed peculiar.

"Just check it, try to jog your memory," Aileen pleaded. "Was there something that seemed peculiar that might be something that you can come forward with and offer a detail to the authorities? It might make a difference."

"To everyone who has been following this devastating story and who has been a part of the search for Antoinette, who showed up at the vigil, who's contributed to our GoFundMe account… I just want to say a deep thank you because it's so meaningful to me and our family."
